thread: Arjun Patel: FYI. Just got a high-priority escalation from Parkside (acct). They've been seeing a surge of 'invented facts' in responses since last night's rollout. Customer says answers now include specific dates, names, and citations that are flat-out wrong.
thread_continued: Arjun Patel: Example they pasted — simple Q: 'When was the Mendel dataset published?' Model answered with a confident year and a DOI that doesn't exist. They attached full request/response, I copied below.
thread_example:
```
POST /v1/generate
{
    "model": "stable-3.1.7",
    "input": "When was the Mendel dataset published?",
    "temperature": 0.0
}

Response:
"The Mendel dataset was first published in 2017 (DOI:10.5555/mendel.2017.032) by the Genomics Lab at U-South."
```
thread_followup: Maya Chen: that's concerning. Parkside said the same prompt used to return vague 'no record' or 'I don't know' in stable-3.0.x, not a fabricated DOI. Any deploy notes that could affect safety filters or temperature defaults?
thread_eng: Liam Torres: Deploy-bot shows a config-only rollout at 2026-03-05T02:14 UTC for stable-3.1.7. No weight changes, but we did push a new tokenization table and a quantization fallback patch for some 8-bit kernels. Could that alter how the model hallucinates?
thread_deploybot: deploy-bot: Deployed stable-3.1.7 to prod pool (all regions) — change: tokenizer updates + q8-fallbacks. Release: patch-2026-03-05. Rollout id 3.1.7-rc5.
thread_investigate: Elena Ruiz: tagging infra + ml. Initial theories: 1) tokenizer change shifted byte-level alignment causing different context parsing, 2) quantization fallback path exposed a weight path that encourages confident but incorrect assertions, or 3) we accidentally enabled a new prompt-prepend that injects authoritative-sounding templates.
thread_repro:
Maya Chen: I repro'd locally using the exact request. With stable-3.0.9 I get 'I don't have data on that dataset'. With stable-3.1.7 I get a confident fabricated citation. Repro steps:
- curl to /v1/generate model=stable-3.0.9 temp=0.0 -> safe result
- curl to /v1/generate model=stable-3.1.7 temp=0.0 -> fabricated DOI
I've attached the raw HAR and the request IDs (req-park-4932).
thread_action: Arjun Patel: Parkside is pushing for rollback or immediate mitigation (they're blocking a demo). Customer asked for: rollback to prior behavior OR a mitigation strategy. They've already turned up monitoring and flagged 12 production requests that caused downstream customer-facing content.
thread_questions: Liam Torres: quick Qs for CS — did Parkside change their prompt or system messages on their side? Any evidence of different user input?
thread_cs_reply: Arjun Patel: they've provided the exact prompt (weirdly it's the same). They explicitly set temperature=0 and max_tokens low. No client-side template changes. They did update to new SDK yesterday but only in the client, and logs show same http request payloads.
thread_suspicions: Elena Ruiz: can we confirm whether the tokenizer update changed special-token indices? If the model sees a shifted context window it might hallucinate to fill perceived gaps. Also ask infra to check if fallback q8 path used different attention kernels that amplify deterministic lexical plugins.
thread_next_steps:
Liam Torres: proposed immediate steps:
1) Scoped rollback of tokenizer table for Parkside's customer pool or pin them to stable-3.0.x as a short-term fix.
2) Re-run a focused regression suite of ~200 'fact-check' prompts across 3.0.x and 3.1.7 to quantify regression.
3) Turn on logging of model execution path (quantization path, kernel selection) for req-park-4932 range.
4) Ask CS to escalate mitigation (webhook to sanitize citations) while we triage.
thread_assign: Elena Ruiz: I'm taking ownership of 1 & 3. Liam, can you run the regression suite and share diff by EOD? Maya, can you coordinate rollback approval with PMs and legal (customer data)? Arjun — keep customer updated with these bullet points.
thread_customer_message: Arjun Patel: Message I sent to customer: 'We see your report and prioritize it. We're running a targeted regression and will propose a rollback or mitigation within 4 hours. For now we recommend disabling auto-citation parsing on your side (strip DOI-looking tokens) until we confirm root cause.' :rotating_light:
thread_notes: Maya Chen: small note — this looks different from prior hallucination tickets: it's deterministic at temp=0, and tied specifically to the new deploy (not prompt drift). Also customer provided samples showing the model invents names of labs and dates in the same pattern across unrelated queries.
thread_close: Liam Torres: regression run initial results: 180/200 prompts show increased factual hallucinations (3.0.x: 12/200, 3.1.7: 68/200 flagged). Attaching diff report link: https://internal.reports/redwood/regressions/3.1.7-vs-3.0x-parkside\n\nElena Ruiz: rolling rollback for Parkside's pool now. Will post update when rollback completes.
thread_resolution: deploy-bot: Rollback applied for customer pool parkside (pinned to stable-3.0.9) — change id rb-1769009999-1. Time: 2026-03-05T06:12 UTC.
thread_followup2: Arjun Patel: Parkside confirmed their demo worked after rollback. They're still asking for postmortem and permanent fix. I'll open a support ticket and schedule a sync next week. Thanks all.
thread_footer: Elena Ruiz: opening a follow-up PR to revert tokenizer table change and add a canary check for 'spurious-citation' pattern in our model-eval suite. Assigned to ml-quality. Marking this P1 and adding to incident log.
